beats.text: You think attractive people are mean. It's a statistics trick!
Let's simulate it. Four hundred people. Looks and kindness are totally random. No link at all.
Now you only date people who are attractive enough, kind enough, or both. Watch what happens.
Among the ones left, the better looking they are, the meaner they get!
Because the mean and plain ones never made your list. So the hot ones you meet don't need to be nice to get there.
It's called Berkson's paradox. It's not that hot people are mean. It's who you filtered out.

ask: SEND THIS TO SOMEONE WHO DATES JERKS.
sources: Berkson (1946), Limitations of the application of fourfold table analysis to hospital data, Biometrics Bulletin 2(3), 47–53 – selection on a combination of two traits creates a spurious negative correlation between them (Berkson's paradox / collider bias).
Ellenberg (2014), How Not to Be Wrong: The Power of Mathematical Thinking – the 'why are handsome men jerks?' illustration of Berkson's paradox.

Simulation in this video: 400 people, looks and kindness drawn independently and uniformly (correlation −0.01); keeping only people with looks + kindness above a threshold leaves 209 people with a correlation of −0.54.
